name: Adults — digital interventions for ADHD/autism
description: Original review: digital interventions in adults with ADHD and/or autism.

a.label: Nova 2 Lite
a.prompt_suffix:
RATER NOTES — apply these strictly; they are your most common mistakes:
1. has_adults: parents, carers, teachers, clinicians, university/college students, employees, military, and any general-adult or unspecified-age clinical sample COUNT AS ADULTS (has_adults=yes, has_under_18=no). A sample described only as 'people/individuals/adults with autism/ADHD' with no under-18 cue is has_adults=yes. Reserve 'unspecified' only when there is NO age or population cue at all. A study of children PLUS their parents is BOTH (has_adults=yes and has_under_18=yes).
2. neurotypes: assign adhd / autistic / audhd ONLY when the studied SAMPLE is formally diagnosed with or selected for it. Broad populations — 'mental health conditions', 'disabilities', 'ADHD-spectrum problems', mood disorders, or a general/mixed clinical group — are neither_adhd_nor_autistic. Never infer autism/ADHD just because the paper is ABOUT, set in, or mentions those fields.
3. study_type: any study reporting numeric/statistical/mixed results is empirical_with_results, even small pilot/acceptability/feasibility studies — do NOT call these qualitative_only_study (reserve that for interview/thematic studies with NO quantitative result). A paper that only PROPOSES or DESIGNS a system/tool without evaluating it is proposal; a single/very-small-N report is case_study; an opinion/editorial/perspective is commentary.
4. intervention_type: a technology used ONLY to assess, measure, monitor, detect, or screen (e.g. a continuous-performance test, a signal-quality tool, a diagnostic classifier) is no_intervention — NOT a software type. But when an intervention IS actually delivered and is clearly digital, commit to the specific type (mobile_app / web_app / software_tool) rather than 'unspecified'.
